regime_context: The TSX detector shows broad but non-dominant leadership concentrated in Base Metals & Copper, with precious metals also eligible; the absolute-trend gate is validated for this market (gate_helps=true), but cross-sectional momentum has no forward edge and the track record's direction accuracy is 0.5, so any leans are low-conviction trend/risk-control calls rather than return forecasts.

theses.subject: Base Metals & Copper
theses.thesis: Base Metals & Copper is the top-ranked eligible theme with full breadth and no crowding; the absolute-trend gate is valid for TSX, so an overweight is a trend-following participation call, not a return forecast. Durability is only mixed, keeping conviction low.
evidence: benchmark headline is Base Metals & Copper
theses.dissent: Copper/base metals are cyclical and headline concentration can mark attention tops; mixed hurst means no persistent trend, and the rank itself has near-zero directional edge.

falsifier.text: XBM.TO underperforms S&P/TSX by 5% before the 20-trading-day check.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners shows the cleanest trend-health among eligible themes (trend hurst, high durability, full breadth, not crowded), and the validated absolute-trend gate supports trend-following exposure. This is a low-conviction, checkable overweight.
theses.dissent: XGD.TO is also the proxy for Silver & Royalties, creating overlap; gold miners can reverse on real-yield or dollar moves, and rank is not alpha.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO underperforms S&P/TSX by 5% before the 20-trading-day check.

theses.subject: Telecom
theses.thesis: Telecom fails the absolute-trend gate (ineligible), has zero breadth and the lowest durability_bar, so trend-following discipline argues for no participation. Avoid is not a short; it is a no-participation lean while the trend gate remains failed.
theses.dissent: Telecom is mean-reverting and could stage a sharp defensive or rate-sensitive rebound; avoiding may miss a rapid bounce if breadth turns quickly.

falsifier.text: XCD.TO outperforms S&P/TSX by 5% before the 20-trading-day check.
